label: Guide
menu_lede: Walkthroughs of the parts of this blog that do more than they show. Open one at any time; none of them changes a setting.
reset_note: Tips you marked as understood will appear again as you browse. Nothing else is reset.
welcome: You're finally back! Let's pick up where we left off.
prompt_down: There's more below — scroll down and I'll show you.
prompt_up: Next up is above — scroll back up a little.
prompt_idle: Still with me? There's plenty more below — keep scrolling.
prompt_comments: Nearly at the end — the discussion is just below. Scroll down to join in.
prompt_recommend: Before you go — a few more posts are waiting just above.

intro.title: Hello, I'm your guide
intro.body: I'm the virtual guide of {site}. I'll show you round — how to follow along, where everything is, the tools that make reading easier, and where the discussion happens. Press Let's go to start; you can find me again any time behind the compass in the side tools.

follow.title: Follow the blog
follow.body: New posts, instant notes and announcements, delivered to an inbox on this site — and, if you allow it, as push notifications on this device. It takes a GitHub sign-in and one press.

bell.title: Your inbox is here
bell.body: Everything you follow arrives behind the bell, newest first. Inside it, Manage subscription chooses the topics and the devices that receive push.

ios_push.title: One more step for push on iPhone
ios_push.body: iOS delivers notifications only to sites added to the Home Screen. Add the blog there, open it from its icon, and push starts working. The inbox works either way.

follow_signed.title: Follow the blog
follow_signed.body: New posts, instant notes and announcements, delivered to an inbox on this site — and, if you allow it, as push notifications on this device. You are already signed in, so one press does it.

inbox_manage.title: Your inbox
inbox_manage.body: Everything you follow lands here, newest first. Manage subscription decides what reaches you, and on which devices.

inbox_push.title: Notifications on this device
inbox_push.body: Turn this on to hear the moment something new is published — even with the blog closed.

inbox_topics.title: Choose what reaches you
inbox_topics.body: Posts and instant notes can each be switched off; the inbox and announcements always stay on. Nothing here unfollows you.

inbox_back.title: Back to your notifications
inbox_back.body: This arrow returns to the inbox.

inbox_close.title: All set
inbox_close.body: Press anywhere outside the inbox to close it. The bell opens it again whenever you like.

navbar.title: Everything is one menu away
navbar.body: Posts holds Archives, Tags, Categories and the photo wall. About and Links hold the rest of the site.

navbar_mobile.title: The menu
navbar_mobile.body: Archives, Tags, Categories and the rest of the site are behind this button — the photo wall is under Posts.

masonry.title: The photo wall
masonry.body: Albums of photographs, laid out as a wall. Any photo opens full-size, and many carry the camera settings they were taken with.

notes.title: Instant notes
notes.body: Short updates rise here as bubbles — remarks that do not need a whole post.

banner_scroll.title: Straight to the posts
banner_scroll.body: This arrow takes you past the banner to everything the blog has published.

author.title: Who writes here
author.body: The author, and how much there is to read — posts, categories and tags, each one press away.

author_pager.title: More than one author
author_pager.body: This card turns to each collaborator in turn, with the posts, categories and tags each has written. Press a dot to go to someone directly, or swipe the card.

links.title: Every way in
links.body: Archives by date, Tags and Categories by subject, the photo wall, and the author's GitHub — one press each.

pulse.title: Site activity
pulse.body: Each square is one day of visits over the past year. The deeper the colour, the busier the day.

post.title: Start with this one?
post.body: Every tile is a post — its size follows how much the post has to say, pinned posts come first, and a series is gathered into one band. This one is a good place to begin.

tools.title: Reading tools
tools.body: The gear opens the tools every page has — text size, dark mode, this guide, and the way back to the top.

tools_font.title: Text size
tools_font.body: Makes the text larger; the button below it makes it smaller again. Your choice is kept on every page.

tools_theme.title: Dark or light
tools_theme.body: Switches the whole blog between its dark and light themes.

guide_entry.title: Every guide, whenever you want it
guide_entry.body: The compass in these tools opens every walkthrough, and can bring back the tips you have already dismissed.

tools_top.title: Back to the top
tools_top.body: Shows how much of the page you have read; press it to go straight back to the top.

exif_toggle.title: This photo has camera data
exif_toggle.body: Press the arrow to unfold how it was taken — camera, lens, exposure and the rest.

exif_hover.title: How this photo was taken
exif_hover.body: This card lists the camera, lens and exposure. It appears whenever the pointer rests on a photo like this one, and the image viewer shows it too.

viewer.title: Open any image
viewer.body: Press an image to see it full-size. Zoom in, drag to look around, and move through every image in the post without leaving it.

errorbook.title: Answer before you look
errorbook.body: Try the question yourself first. A right answer stays quiet; a wrong one opens the explanation of why.

code.title: Copy or fold the code
code.body: These buttons appear when the pointer is over a code block. Copy takes the whole block without line numbers; the arrow folds it away.

toc.title: Contents
toc.body: Shows or hides the table of contents. The section you are reading stays highlighted, and any heading is one press away.

comments.title: Join the discussion
comments.body: Comments on this blog are GitHub Discussions. Sign in with GitHub once, and you can comment, reply and react under any post.

recommend.title: Read on
recommend.body: If you enjoyed this post, here is another you might like — picked from the ones most like it.

album_photo.title: Browse the album
album_photo.body: Open a photo to see it full-size, then swipe or use the arrows to move through the whole album.

album_heart.title: Like a photo
album_heart.body: The heart likes a photo with your GitHub account. The first press asks you to sign in, and finishes the like once you are back.

albums.title: Albums
albums.body: Each card is an album. Open one to see its photos laid out as a wall.

search.title: Search the whole blog
search.body: Search looks through the title and full text of every post as you type.

follow.name: Following this blog
follow.desc: New posts in an inbox on this site and as notifications on your device, and how signing in works.
follow.signed_in: You are already signed in as @{login}, so the GitHub steps are done.

published.title: When something new is published
published.body: A new post, instant note or announcement reaches you twice. Your device shows it as a notification, even while the blog is closed, and it waits in the inbox behind the bell in the navigation bar until you have read it.

install_ios.title: Add the blog to your Home Screen
install_ios.body: iPhone and iPad deliver notifications only to a site installed on the Home Screen. In Safari, tap ⋯, then Share, scroll to Add to Home Screen, turn on Open as Web App and tap Add. Then open the blog from its new icon and follow from there. Requires iOS 16.4 or later.

install_mac.title: Keep the blog in your Dock
install_mac.body: Optional on a Mac. In Safari, choose File → Add to Dock… and press Add; the blog then opens in its own window from the Dock. Safari delivers the blog's notifications either way. Requires macOS Sonoma or later.

signin.title: Sign in through giscus
signin.body: Following uses your GitHub account through giscus, the app that also runs the comments. Press Follow, and GitHub asks you to sign in to continue to giscus. With an account already, sign in here and go on to the authorization.

register.title: Create a GitHub account
register.body: Without an account, choose Create an account. Enter an email address, a password and a username, choose your country or region, and press Create account. GitHub then asks you to solve a short puzzle and to type in the code it emails you. The account is free.

authorize.title: Authorize giscus
authorize.body: The first time, GitHub asks whether giscus may verify your GitHub identity, know which resources you can access, and act on your behalf — which is how it posts the comments you write. Press Authorize to return to the blog, signed in. The authorization can be revoked at any time under GitHub Settings → Applications.

allow.title: Follow, and allow notifications
allow.body: Back on the blog, press Follow once more. Your system then asks whether this site may send notifications; choose Allow to receive them on this device. Choosing Block still follows the blog — everything keeps arriving in the inbox, only without the notification. The Follow button then becomes the bell.

comments.name: Comments and sign-in
comments.desc: Joining the discussion under any post with a GitHub account.

thread.title: Comments live on GitHub
thread.body: Each post has its own thread in GitHub Discussions, shown here through giscus. Your comments appear under your GitHub name and avatar, and can also be found, edited or deleted on GitHub itself.

authorize.title: Sign in through giscus
authorize.body: Press Sign in with GitHub in the comment box. GitHub asks you to authorize giscus — to verify your identity, to know which resources you can access and to act on your behalf, which is how it posts what you write. Press Authorize and you return to the post, signed in.

write.title: Write, preview, send
write.body: Type in the box; Markdown works, including code, links and lists. Preview shows the result before you press Comment, and a reply stays attached to the comment it answers.

react.title: React, and stay in the loop
react.body: The smiley adds a reaction instead of a comment. The same sign-in likes photos on the photo wall and follows the blog, so it is the only account this site asks for.

mock.post_body: A cursor that points at the parts of the blog that do more than they show, and says why.
mock.note_title: Re-shot the harbour album this evening
mock.announce_title: The blog now sends push notifications
mock.ios_alert: “{site}” Would Like to Send You Notifications
mock.ios_alert_body: Notifications may include alerts, sounds and icon badges. These can be configured in Settings.
mock.mac_alert: “{host}” would like to send you notifications
mock.mac_alert_body: Notifications may include alerts, sounds and badges. These can be configured in System Settings.
mock.sample_reply: Glad it helped — more on this soon.
